chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

The worst in bargaining and the most unsuccessful in striving is the man who exerts himself in seeking riches although fate does not help him in his aims and consequently he goes from this world in a sorrowful state while in the next world too he will face its ill consequences.
ai.seo_question: Who is considered the worst in bargaining according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes the individual who exhausts their physical and mental faculties chasing unattainable worldly desires as the 'worst in trade,' highlighting the spiritual loss incurred when human effort clashes with divine decree (al-maqadir). This narration serves as a critical Shia ethical teaching on the balance between active striving (juhd) and acceptance of God's will, warning that excessive attachment to transient wealth results in leaving the world with regret and entering the Hereafter with the heavy burden of those pursuits.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 430. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

The worst in bargaining and the most unsuccessful in striving is the man who exerts himself in seeking riches although fate does not help him in his aims and consequently he goes from this world in a sorrowful state while in the next world too he will face its ill consequences. [1]
